outcome: sexual function (Female Sexual Function Index - FSFI)
sexual function (Pelvic Organ Prolapse Urinary Incontinence Sexual Questionnaire - PISQ)
cohort: The study included 188 patients diagnosed with stress urinary incontinence (SUI) and pelvic organ prolapse who underwent either anterior colporrhaphy or transobturator tape (TOT) surgery.
finding: Both anterior colporrhaphy and transobturator tape (TOT) surgeries were found to be effective in treating stress urinary incontinence and improving PISQ scores, with TOT surgery specifically showing a significant increase in sexual satisfaction, although no significant difference was observed between the two surgery types regarding overall PISQ or FSFI scores.
